claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 11 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you at home.

Now I need to ask you about your residency status:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex - meaning you're the one looking after him and providing for his needs (such as food, clothes, accommodation, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm the one looking after him and providing for his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just one more question to ensure I have all the necessary information:

**Do you have any circumstances that might affect eligibility, such as:**
- Alex being in hospital or care for an extended period?
- You or your partner having pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- You recently moving to the UK?
- Any other unusual circumstances?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - it's been about 15 weeks or so. He's been there for quite some time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important information. That does affect the situation, so I need to ask a follow-up question:

**During the time Alex has been in hospital (the 15 weeks), have you been regularly spending money on him - for example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for his use?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I... I'm not really sure. It's been difficult with everything going on, and I haven't really kept track of whether I've been spending on those kinds of things regularly or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it's a difficult situation and these details can be hard to keep track of during such a challenging time.

Let me also ask: **Has Alex had any breaks from his hospital stay? For example, has he come home for visits, even briefly, during these 15 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't been able to come home at all during this time. He's been in the hospital the whole period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I understand this is a difficult time for you and your family.

Based on what you've told me, let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit:

**Summary of your situation:**
- Alex is 11 years old and normally lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for him and provide for his needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- However, Alex has been in hospital continuously for approximately 15 weeks
- You're unsure whether you've been regularly spending money on him during his hospital stay

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into hospital for more than 12 weeks, Child Benefit payments are usually affected. After 12 weeks, you're generally no longer entitled to Child Benefit **unless** there's an exception - such as if you're regularly spending money on the child during their hospital stay.

Since you've indicated that you're not sure whether you've been regularly spending money on Alex during his 15-week hospital stay, and this is a key factor in determining whether you can continue to receive Child Benefit after the 12-week period, I cannot make a definite determination of eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**My recommendation:** I would strongly suggest contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Review your individual circumstances in detail
- Help you understand whether any spending you've done counts as "regularly spending money" on Alex
- Advise you on your entitlement and what documentation might be needed

I hope Alex recovers soon, and I wish you and your family all the best during this difficult time.
